title: Optimized protocol for analysis of neural stem proliferation in human-pluripotent-stem-cell-derived cerebral organoids
protocol: Thaw Vitronectin on ice or at 4°C for 8–12 hours.
Swirl the vial to ensure that the contents are fully dispersed.
Add 60 μL of Vitronectin into microcentrifuge tubes.
Calculate the working concentration using the formula: Working Concentration = Coating Concentration × Culture Surface Area / Volume Required for Surface Area.
Determine the dilution factor with the formula: Dilution Factor = Stock Concentration (0.5 mg/mL) / Working Concentration.
Prepare Vitronectin solution at a 100× dilution to achieve a working concentration of 0.5 μg/ml.
Dilute VTN 100-fold in DMEM/F12 for subsequent plate coating.
Add 60 μl of VTN to 6 mL DMEM/F12 in a 15 mL conical tube.
Pipette up and down to blend contents completely.
Add 1 ml of VTN working solution to each well of the 6-well plate.
Gently shake the plate to ensure even distribution of VTN mixture along the bottom of the well.
Seal the coated plate with parafilm to avoid reagent evaporation and bacterial contamination.
Incubate the 6-well plate at 4°C for a minimum of 12 h and a maximum of 1 week.
Warm hPSC medium, EDTA, and DMEM/F12 in a 37°C water bath for about 20 minutes.
Completely remove all media from the plate.
Wash the cells with 1 × DPBS.
Add 1 ml of EDTA to each well, enough to cover the surface entirely.
Incubate the cells at 37°C for 1.5–2 minutes.
Remove EDTA by gentle aspiration once cell colonies become bright and dissociated.
Slowly add 1 ml DMEM/F12 to each well and gently swirl the plates.
Remove DMEM/F12 by gentle aspiration to avoid disruption of attached cell colonies.
Add 1 ml of hPSC medium per well, pipette up and down gently.
Take the prepared Vitronectin-coated 6-well plate, remove vitronectin working solution, and add pre-warmed hPSC medium.
Mix the cell suspension with a fresh hPSC medium in the ratio of 1:20-1:30.
Gently shake the plate to ensure an even distribution of cell clusters.
Place the plate into a 37°C/5% CO2 incubator.
Remove all media from wells the next day to eliminate dead cells.
Add 2 mL hPSC medium to each well.
Perform daily half-medium exchanges until cells approach 70-80% confluency by gently aspirating approximately 1 mL of the medium and adding an additional 1 mL of fresh hPSC medium.
Passage freshly thawed hPSCs at least twice before starting neural differentiation.
Add ROCK inhibitor to a final concentration of 2 μM in E8 medium when thawing iPSCs.
Warm Dispase, DMEM/F12, hPSC medium, and Neural Induction Medium in a 37°C water bath for about 20 minutes.
Aspirate all medium from the plate.
Wash cells with 1× DPBS.
Add 1 ml of Dispase to each well and incubate at 37°C for 3–4 minutes.
Remove the Dispase from each well.
Wash the wells with 1 ml DMEM/F12 by gentle shaking.
Remove the DMEM/F12.
Add another 2 ml DMEM/F12 medium to each well.
Scrape down the colonies in the vertical and horizontal direction with a 1 mL pipette tip.
Gently mix the cell suspension with DMEM/F12 medium.
Transfer the liquid from the well to a 15-mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge for 1 min at 800 × g.
Remove the supernatant by gentle aspiration.
Add hPSC medium and Neural Induction Medium equally to mix the colonies up.
Transfer the cell suspension to a flask.
Incubate it at 37°C with 5% CO2.
On day 1, observe EBs under microscope.
Replace half of the medium with fresh Neural Induction Medium.
Measure the volume of liquid by drawing the liquid up into the pipette tip and reading the scale on the pipette.
Gently return the liquid back to the flask.
Add SB431542 and DMH1 with a 1:5000 ratio (final concentration 2 μM).
Return the plate to the incubator for further culturing.
On day 2 to day 6, replace half of the Neural Induction Medium daily containing 2 μM SB431542 and DMH1.
Liquefy aliquots of Matrigel at 2°C–8°C refrigerator one day before use.
Chill all plasticware that comes in contact with Matrigel at −20°C or on ice for at least half an hour before use.
Keep Matrigel on ice to prevent premature solidification.
Trim the Parafilm to a smaller square with sterile scissors, then place the square of parafilm into a 60-mm culture dish.
Place both sides of the Parafilm under UV light in biological safety cabinet for 30 minutes before use.
Use a wide-bore 200-μL pipette tip to transfer EBs to parafilm (only one for each position).
Cut the end of a 1mL pipette tip to an opening of approximately 4mm.
Cut the end of a 200-μL pipette tip to an opening of approximately 1.5mm.
Flame the cut part of the pipette tips to make the caliber smooth.
Aspirate excess medium from each EB using a standard 200-μL pipette tip, removing no more than 15 drops at a time.
Add 20 μL of chilled Matrigel droplet to each EB with a wide-bore 200-μL pipette tip.
Gently stir the droplet with a 10-μL pipette tip to reposition the EB to the center of the Matrigel droplet.
Place the dish containing droplets in a 37 °C/5% CO2 incubator for 30 minutes to allow Matrigel droplets to polymerize.
Transfer the Matrigel droplets to a 6-well plate using sterile forceps and Parafilm.
Wash the droplets off the Parafilm with cerebral organoids differentiation medium from a 1-mL pipette tip.
Dispense 7–8 tissue droplets with 6–7 mL cerebral organoids differentiation medium per well of a 6-well plate.
Place the plate in a static 37 °C/5% CO2 incubator.
Gently pipette medium up and down 2–3 times without touching Matrigel-embedded organoids every other day to prevent attachment of droplets.
Observe the embedded tissue under the microscope after 3 days.
Refresh half of the medium by using a 5-mL serological pipette at the slowest setting.
Perform a half-medium exchange every 4 days as described in step 35.
Monitor organoids for morphology at each media change under a light microscope.
Fix organoids with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Transfer organoids into 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tubes using a wide-bore 1-mL pipette tip.
Centrifuge to remove the organoid medium.
Wash organoids with 1 ml of 1 × DPBS.
Add 1 ml of 4% PFA for fixation and place at 4°C for 15–20 hours or at 20°C-25°C for 4 hours.
Dehydrate the organoids with 30% sucrose solution.
Centrifuge the organoids at 300 × g for 3–5 seconds.
Remove the supernatant PFA.
Wash the organoids three times with 1 mL of 1× DPBS.
Add 1 mL of 30% sucrose solution to the organoids.
Place the tube containing the organoids in a 4°C refrigerator for 8–12 hours.
Aspirate the completely dehydrated organoids using a wide-bore 200 μL pipette tip.
Place the aspirated organoids in the center of a pre-cooled sample holder.
Quickly embed the organoids with approximately 500 μL OCT Compound™.
Place the embedded organoids on a quick-freezing platform for 3–5 minutes.
Transfer the sample holder to an adaptation box at −20°C.
Insert the sample holder into the sample platform after 1 minute.
Set the slice thickness to 10 μm.
Attach the sliced organoids to poly-lysine-treated glass slides.
Place the attached slices into pathological slide boxes.
Store the slides in a −80°C freezer for long-term storage.
Rinse the slices with 1× DPBS three times, each rinse lasting 10 minutes, to remove residual OCT Compound™.
Incubate for 1 hour at 20°C–25°C in Blocking Buffer (1% Triton + 5% donkey serum in 1 × DPBS).
Remove the Blocking Buffer from poly-lysine-treated glass slides containing the organoids with a 200 μL pipette tip.

Incubate with respective primary antibodies diluted in primary antibody vehicle solution (0.2% Triton + 5% donkey serum in 1 × DPBS) for 30 minutes at 20°C–25°C and then transfer them to 4°C for 8-12 hours.
Wash the slides three times with 1 × DPBS, 10 minutes each time, to remove the primary antibody/vehicle solution mix.
Incubate the slides in appropriate secondary antibodies diluted in vehicle solution (5% donkey serum in 1 × DPBS) for 1 hour at 20°C–25°C.
Rinse the slides three times with 1 × DPBS, 10 minutes each time, to remove secondary antibodies.
Mount the slides with the anti-fluorescence quenching mounting medium.
Open ImageJ software.
Load pre-processed images stained with Ki67 and Hoechst by Drag&Drop.
Click “Image>Color>Merge Channels” to open a dialog.
Assign the Hoechst-stained image to the Blue channel.
Assign the Ki67-stained image to the Red channel.
Click “OK” to create a new composite image with RGB format.
Select the composite image.
Click the tab “Image>Adjust>Color balance” to adjust brightness and contrast of the selected channel only.
Open ImageJ software.
Calibrate ImageJ software with measurements in micrometers for the images.
Load an image with a known scale bar and same magnification as organoid photographs.
Draw a line along the scale bar using the “straight” line selection tool.
Go to “Analyze>set scale” and input the pixel distance of the line drawn.
Fill in the "Known distance" (100 μm) without units.
Define the unit of length as μm.
Click on “Global” to apply calibration to all images in this session.
Click “OK” to confirm settings.
Quantify the length of apical and basal membranes using the “Freehand selections” tool.
Mark along the apical surface of VZ with the “Freehand selections” tool.
Measure the length of the marked area to determine the length of the apical membrane.
Mark along the basal surface of VZ with the “Freehand selections” tool.
Measure the length of the marked area to determine the length of the basal membrane.
Quantify the area of ventricle-like region using the “Freehand selections” tool.
Mark the ventricle-like region within the neuroepithelium loop.
Measure the marked area to determine the ventricle-like region's area in μm².
Quantify the total loop region using the “Freehand selections” tool.
Mark the entire loop region of the neuroepithelial loop.
Measure the marked area to determine the total loop region's area in μm².
Calculate the area of loop tissue by subtracting ventricle-like area from the total loop region's area.
